original_question: Let x in (X = Spec(R), Delta) be a germ of a klt singularity, let a_bullet be a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals, let c = lct(X, Delta; a_bullet), and let LCP(X, Delta + c a_bullet) be the set of valuations v with c = A_{X,Delta}(v) / v(a_bullet). Are all valuations in this set quasi-monomial, and more strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) -> X such that LCP(X, Delta + c a_bullet) is contained in QM(Y, E) and forms a cone over a connected convex set?
target_in_paper: Problem 37 in §4.2.2 ("Graded ideal sequence"): the structural question about the full set LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) of valuations computing the log canonical threshold of a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals on a klt singularity.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It has the right ambient local setup x ∈ (X = Spec(R), Δ), the right object a• (a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals), the correct threshold c = lct(X, Δ; a•), the correct definition of LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) via c = A_{X,Δ}(v)/v(a•), and it asks exactly the two questions that appear in the paper: whether every such valuation is quasi-monomial, and whether, more strongly, the whole set sits inside QM(Y, E) on one log smooth model and is a cone over a connected convex set.
missing_details: The paper states this as Problem 37, not as a conjecture.
The setup is introduced immediately before the problem in item 36 of §4.2.2, and explicitly assumes c = lct(X, Δ; a•) < +∞.
The official definition is LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) := { v ∈ Val_{X,x} | c = A_{X,Δ}(v) / v(a•) }, so the ambient valuation space Val_{X,x} should be named in a stand-alone formulation.
In the stronger version, the paper explicitly requires LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) ⊆ QM(Y, E) for one log smooth model (Y, E) → X, and then asks that this whole subset be a cone over a connected convex set.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to spell out that QM(Y, E) denotes the quasi-monomial valuations associated to the log smooth pair (Y, E).
The notation v(a•) is used in the paper without expansion at this point; for a stand-alone question, one should retain it as the standard valuation of a graded sequence or define it explicitly.
The nearby context records the known partial results: [JM12] proves nonemptiness of LCP(X, Δ + c·a•), and [Xu20] proves that it contains at least one quasi-monomial valuation.

The immediately following Problem 38 asks for a valuation in LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) with finitely generated Gr_v R, or even a Kollár valuation; this is not equivalent to Problem 37, but it clarifies the intended narrow scope.
refined_question:
Let x ∈ (X = Spec(R), Δ) be a germ of a klt singularity, let a• be a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals, and set c := lct(X, Δ; a•) < +∞. Define
LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) := { v ∈ Val_{X,x} | c = A_{X,Δ}(v) / v(a•) }.
Is every valuation in LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) quasi-monomial? More strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) → X such that LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) ⊆ QM(Y, E) and this subset is a cone over a connected convex set?
justification: This is the paper’s Problem 37, stated in §4.2.2 after item 36 fixes exactly the notation appearing in your draft. The paragraph immediately before Problem 37 says that [JM12] proves nonemptiness of LCP(X, Δ + c·a•), and that [Xu20] proves the existence of at least one quasi-monomial valuation in that set. Problem 37 then asks precisely for the structure of the entire set of lct-computing valuations, first in the weaker quasi-monomiality form and then in the stronger single-log-smooth-model/connected-convex-cone form. Problem 38 is a neighboring strengthening about finite generation and Kollár valuations, so it is useful context but not an equivalent reformulation. Your draft therefore already captures the intended target almost verbatim; the main refinements are to restore the exact item-36 notation and keep the official two-part Problem 37 framing.
